dataProvenance: Locations and short descriptions based on published gazetteer values; the list of sites is a predefined mission dataset.

points.name: Acidalia Planitia (central plain)
points.description: Centre of the large, dark plain in Mars's northern lowlands. Very flat terrain, interpreted as a basin that collected sediment from the surrounding highlands. A reference site for the whole study region.

points.name: Acidalia Colles
points.description: Cluster of small hills and knobs about 360 km long. Gullies have been observed on the hills.

points.name: Face on Mars (Cydonia mesa)
points.description: Roughly 2 km mesa that looked like a face in a 1976 Viking 1 image. Later, higher-resolution images show an ordinary eroded hill, a good example of how lighting can create false patterns.

points.name: Crater with candidate mud-volcano deposit
points.description: Impact crater about 11.6 km across with a deposit on its south-western rim that some studies interpret as a possible mud volcano. The interpretation is a candidate, not a confirmed result.

points.name: Lomonosov Crater (southern rim)
points.description: Rim area of Lomonosov Crater, a 153 km impact crater near the northern edge of the plain. The crater centre lies just beyond the study region, so this site is on its southern rim.

points.name: Kunowsky Crater
points.description: Impact crater about 67 km across in the northern part of the plain.

points.name: Acidalia Mensa
points.description: Remnant mesa-like landform in the plain. Its margin has been interpreted as a possible ancient shoreline.

points.name: Bamberg Crater
points.description: Impact crater about 58 km across near the highland-lowland transition. Gullies have been imaged on its walls.
